subject: Next steps: vendor setup packet, PO vs card, and marketplace interest
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@clearview.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: vendor setup packet, PO vs card, and marketplace interest

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for your time on the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get procurement moving on our side:

1) Commercial path you mentioned: preferred route is a standard PO submitted to our finance team, but you said you might also be able to use a company card for pilot spend. Can you confirm which you prefer for the initial POC (PO vs card)?

2) Vendor paperwork: I attached the vendor setup packet we typically send to procurement. It includes the list of required docs (W-9/W-8, bank routing instructions or vendor portal info, certificate of insurance if needed). If ClearView uses a vendor portal, please send the portal link and any onboarding steps.

3) Marketplace: you asked about AWS Marketplace / GCP marketplace listings — are you interested in procurement through marketplace (subscription) or direct P-card/PO? Marketplace often shortens legal review but requires marketplace procurement ID.

4) Timeline: you mentioned a legal/commercial review by EoW — if we get the vendor packet + preferred purchase path by Thursday, we can accelerate setup and schedule the pilot for the week of Sep 7.

Attachments: Redwood_Vendor_Setup_Packet.pdf (packet outline), W9_Instructions.txt

Next steps: would you be able to confirm PO vs card preference and send the portal link (if applicable) by Thu 9/2? Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0134

---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)

From: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@clearview.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: vendor setup packet, PO vs card, and marketplace interest

Jonas —

Appreciate the notes and the packet. Short answers from procurement here: we typically run pilots on a company card to avoid a formal PO for small initial spend (under $5k), but larger purchases require a PO. For this POC I think card will be easiest.

We do have a vendor portal (https://vendors.clearview.com/onboard). I'll loop in procurement@clearview.com (cc’ed) — they’ll need the packet and a copy of your W-9. We also require a vendor contact and a bank ACH form if we end up doing PO payments.

I can get the procurement folks to start the portal intake today; they may still ask for the vendor packet to be emailed directly to procurement@clearview.com.

Samantha Jenkins
Head of Data Partnerships, ClearView Analytics
samantha.jenkins@clearview.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: vendor setup packet, PO vs card, and marketplace interest

Thanks Samantha — card for the POC works fine. A couple quick clarifications so procurement has exactly what they need:

- For the vendor portal: do you prefer we upload the packet directly into the portal or email it to procurement@clearview.com? If upload, please confirm we should create a Redwood Inference vendor record under: Redwood Inference / EIN: 12-3456789.
- For ACH/bank details: if the portal supports secure bank upload we’ll use that; otherwise Marissa (cc’d) will send a secure bank form via your portal link or encrypted email.
- Marketplace: if you think long-term purchasing may go through AWS Marketplace, please let us know and we’ll put together the marketplace SKU/pricing summary — marketplace can be faster for procurement/legal but is optional for pilots.

If it's helpful, Marissa from Sales Ops can push the vendor packet + W-9 directly to procurement and confirm next steps. Marissa — could you prepare the W-9 and vendor packet for portal upload and share an upload-ready PDF?

Thanks,
Jonas
